summary: Tenant affinity rotation causes repeated fallback cycling during canary
description: Issue summary: During a staged canary for redwood-open-7b-v2 in eu-west, some tenant traffic entered a rapid cycle of fallback routing between the canary and primary model. The cycling manifested as increased 5xxs and elevated token latency for the affected tenant. Impact: NovelHealth reported degraded inference success for ~3% of requests (rate limited cohort) and intermittent timeouts for streaming sessions. User-facing: chat session interruptions and duplicated partial responses. Environment: prod cluster eu-west; Dedicated pool ID: ded-eu-24; Canary rollout started 2026-03-09 21:00 UTC. Steps to reproduce: 1) Tenant uses long-lived session with HTTP/2 multiplexed streams and client-side retry logic; 2) Send overlapping streaming requests (concurrent chat turns) under the tenant scoped token; 3) Observe alternating model assignment in x-Redwood-Model header across successive requests; 4) Monitor request traces in tracing service and check serving-runtime logs for fallback triggers. Logs/snippets: - edge-proxy timed out handshake with routing-service: "ctx deadline exceeded" - routing-service emitted fallback decision due to stale-session-mapping and returned HTTP 302 to edge with fallback route - serving-runtime returned 503 with message "KV cache mismatch: session affinity lost"
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Configure tenant token for NovelHealth on Dedicated pool ded-eu-24. 2. Start canary rollout for redwood-open-7b-v2 with canary weight 5%. 3. From a single client create two concurrent streaming requests over HTTP/2 multiplexing. 4. Note x-Redwood-Session and x-Redwood-Model headers in responses; repeat until affinity alternates. 5. Check Edge, routing-service, and session-store traces within the same 5-minute window.
comments: 2026-03-10 08:12 - Support (Aisha Khan): Customer reports inconsistent model assignment during canary; they see repeated fallback between canary and stable model. Asking for immediate escalation.

2026-03-10 08:45 - SRE (Marco Rivera): Reproduced in controlled environment with HTTP/2 multiplexing. Observed session mapping TTLs refreshed out-of-order when parallel streams hit different edge nodes.

2026-03-10 12:30 - Customer (Nov elHealth, Support Contact: Jenna Li): This is affecting our live customer chats; can you provide a temporary mitigation? We're seeing duplicate partial messages in the UI.

2026-03-11 02:05 - Support (Aisha Khan): Provided mitigation: advise client to disable aggressive retry and reduce concurrent streaming to single active stream per session. Also requested routing-service logs and edge-proxy metrics. Customer applied mitigation and saw partial improvement.

2026-03-12 16:20 - Eng (Priya Desai): Found correlating alert: edge-proxy connection churn spike at 21:03 UTC coinciding with canary weight increase. Possible race in session-store write-through causing stale affinity tokens.
2026-03-13 09:40 - SRE (Marco Rivera): Implemented canary holdback in eu-west region to stop additional traffic to canary while we patch session reconciliation. Monitoring for error rate regression.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: HTTP/2 multiplexing + edge-proxy sticky mapping TTL race can cause session-store to persist inconsistent affinity (token A points to canary on node X while token B for same session points to primary on node Y).

Trace evidence: trace_id=tr-7b2c showed request1 routed to canary then request2 (same session) routed to stable; both requests updated session-store almost simultaneously with different model assignments. Timestamp skew ~12ms between writes.
Metrics: 503s and token latency increased by 4x for affected tenant during the rolling window; session-store write latency spikes to 120ms (baseline 8-12ms).
Reproducible: Yes in a lab with HTTP/2 multiplexed streams and artificially injected node churn. Not reproducible with single-stream clients.

Root cause likely interaction of: (a) edge-proxy selecting upstreams with stale local cache, (b) routing-service fallback policy triggers when session-store read indicates incompatible model, (c) session-store write-merge is last-write-wins without causality checks.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied: temporarily froze canary weight and enabled per-tenant session serialization for NovelHealth (requests for same session routed through same edge node). Long term: engineering to land session-store merge versioning (PR referenced) and add stronger affinity reconciliation in routing-service. Rollout notes: holdback enacted 2026-03-12 16:40 UTC; observed error rate drop to baseline within 45 minutes for the affected cohort. Follow-ups: INT ticket created for session-store versioning (INT-4128), and edge-proxy reconnect logic patch scheduled (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/112). Customer agreed to rollback mitigation after permanent fix is deployed.
